title: Public Information, Private Expertise, and Lender Specialization
abstract: Why do lenders specialize in specific industries rather than diversify? Exploiting the SBA's 2014 credit-scoring mandate, which applied to most guaranteed loans but left one program exempt, I show that standardized scores reduced specialization by 12.7 percent as lenders entered new sectors and reallocated portfolios. Yet public information crowds out private expertise: in previously specialized industries, post-reform defaults rise by 11 percent of the pre-policy rate while competitive entry holds spreads flat. A Bartik shift-share IV confirms that remaining specialization causally lowers defaults, deepens repeat borrowing, and reduces spreads for repeat borrowers, reflecting informational complementarities rather than hold-up.
